title: MSA/DPA variant signoff and escrow path
summary: Redwood AE/SE walked Helitrope through proposed MSA variant, DPA options for data residency, and an escrow-like billing segmentation for restricted keys. Customer requested narrow DPA language around AI model outputs and stronger audit log commitments; security asked for KMS-HSM integration and proof of SOC 2 Type II evidence. Agreed next step: Redwood to send redline bundle and a short technical appendix, legal-to-legal sync scheduled for 11/10.

Schedule legal-to-legal sync for 2025-11-10 10:00 AM ET

transcript:
Meeting header: 2025-11-06 15:00 PST / 18:00 EST, Duration: ~52 minutes. Attendees: Elena Park (Redwood AE), Marco Ruiz (Redwood SE), Nadia Kim (Redwood CSM), Priya Shah (Heliotrope - Procurement), Evan Cole (Heliotrope - Legal), Lindsey Moore (Heliotrope - Security), Aaron Li (Heliotrope - Platform).

[00:00] Elena: Hey everyone, thanks for carving time. Quick roll call — we've got legal and security, great. Main goals today: walk through the MSA redline variants, present two DPA flavors, and a proposal Helio asked about — an escrow-like billing separation for privileged keying.

[00:18] Priya: Hi. Yes, procurement wants to understand the execution path so we can hit finance approval. We're sensitive to vendor risk and want clarity on the billing pathway if privileged keys are required.

[00:30] Marco: Cool. I'll start with a very short technical overview so the legal asks have context. Redwood supports three deployment modes — hosted API, dedicated pools, and private (VPC / on-prem). For privileged workloads we usually recommend Private with customer-managed KMS or HSM; that lets the customer keep keys. There's a small latency delta versus hosted — usually single-digit ms but depends on network.

[00:58] Lindsey: Single-digit what? We need numbers. We run low-latency trading signals; even 10–20ms is material.

[01:10] Marco: Understood. For a Private deployment with co-located inference, our internal benchmarks show 6–12ms median per-token latency for standard models at 512-token windows. If you route through a VPC endpoint it adds network RTT — that's the variable. I'll provide a short benchmark note.

[01:34] Evan: Thanks. On the legal side — we reviewed Redwood's standard MSA. Our general counsel flagged three sections: audit rights, data processing definitions (specifically what constitutes customer data vs. model output), and termination/escrow for privileged keys.

[01:50] Elena: Got it. We prepared two DPA variants — one is the standard data processing annex which preserves some transient logging for performance debugging, the other is a minimized-retention variant that keeps only core telemetry and no conversational logs beyond short-lived caches. We can couple either with KMS integrations.

[02:12] Priya: For procurement we prefer the minimized-retention variant. But we need to be sure the SLA doesn't get voided if we choose that — in other words, we still need 99.9% uptime and measurable traces for incidents.

[02:28] Nadia: We're able to surface token-level cost and latency breakdowns in the Console; for Private we can set up a test tenant so you can verify the dashboard during the pilot.

[02:42] Aaron: Quick technical question — if we supply an HSM and manage the keys, does Redwood have any way to cache keys or is every call escrowed through our KMS? How does that affect throughput?

[02:58] Marco: Good question. When you bring your own KMS/HSM we do not persist key material. We perform per-session key exchange and keep an in-memory ephemeral reference (no key material at rest on our side). That allows local KV caches to use wrapped tokens for performance; however, if you require zero-KV-caching we can run a stricter flow which will increase per-call CPU and add latency. We'll document the latency delta.

[03:24] Lindsey: SOC 2 — we need the latest Type II report and a description of your audit logging. Also want RBAC controls for L2 engineers.

[03:36] Elena: We'll provide SOC 2 Type II and an audit log sample. Our RBAC supports role scoping and token-level entitlements; we'll map those to Helio roles as part of onboarding.

[03:48] Evan: Back to the MSA: escrow language — we don't mean software escrow but rather a billing/entitlement partitioning: if the keys are customer-held or privileged, we want an escrow-like clause to protect continuity if Redwood has a service incident or if we need to spin up with a backup provider. We're not asking Redwood to hand over keys; we want the contract to ensure outputs and continuity. How do you approach that?

[04:12] Elena: Right — we've seen two patterns. One is an operational continuity clause with a defined remediation timeline and a temporary dedicated throughput allocation (kind of prepaid buffer) in cases of vendor outage. The other is a more formal escrow of artifacts (e.g., exported model weights or container images) — which for commercial open models is possible but for third-party licensed models may be restricted.

[04:36] Priya: We're less concerned on weights but more about being able to run with another provider in a constrained window. So we need a clause that says Redwood will provide an export of customer-specific metadata, prompt logs (if retained), and a technical handoff plan. Also some billing protections if a service-level miss occurs.

[04:56] Nadia: For pilot customers we can offer a 'split-billing' approach temporarily: a portion of the spend is designated for privileged-key usage and escrowed on the ledger so it's not subject to immediate refunds — it acts like a ring-fenced buffer. We don't like the term escrow in legal because it means third-party trust, but functionally it achieves a reserved capacity.

[05:18] Evan: We will need precise contractual language. Procurement will push back on non-specific terms like 'temporary allocation' unless we have durations and penalties.

[05:30] Marco: Example: if Redwood misses an SLA for more than X minutes in a month, we commit a reserved throughput of Y tokens per minute for up to Z days for the customer to run a failover. There's also an option to pre-stage a canary image in your cloud tenancy. That adds complexity but is doable.

[05:54] Aaron: Pre-staging a canary image — would that be in our account or Redwood's? We are strict about external code in our VPC.

[06:06] Marco: Best practice is pre-staging in your account with the image pulled from a signed artifact repository we control; we provide the build output and a signed manifest. That lets your infra team validate before execution.

[06:22] Priya: On billing — procurement wants acceptance criteria tied to milestone payments. Can we map the pilot to an acceptance matrix and gate initial reserved capacity upon signature?

[06:34] Elena: Yes. We can propose a pilot SOW that lays out milestones: onboarding, 2-week functional test, 4-week performance acceptance. Payment schedule can be milestone-based. We'll include an acceptance checklist.

[06:46] Evan: A couple more legal items: indemnity around model outputs is a hot point. We want explicit carve-outs for customer-provided prompts and data. Also clarifying ownership of model improvements from our proprietary data.

[07:02] Elena: Our standard MSA states customer retains ownership of customer data; model improvements language can be adjusted to carve out customer prompt-derived fine-tuning if that's material. We'll propose a clause.

[07:12] Lindsey: Also, audit logs — we need retention window options and an export API to push logs to our SIEM. We can't have the logs only in Redwood's UI.

[07:24] Nadia: We have a log-export API and S3 sink options. For Private we can do direct syslog forwarding as well. We'll share docs.

[07:36] Priya: Timeline? We need legal signoff by 11/21 to get on the December vendor intake board. Is that feasible?

[07:46] Elena: With a tight redline cycle we can aim for that. Proposed schedule: send redlines by 11/08; legal-to-legal sync 11/10; procurement & finance finalization 11/15–11/19; target signature before 11/21. Does that align?

[07:58] Evan: Works if the redlines are clear and we get responses within 48 hours after the sync.

[08:06] Marco: I'll note two technical risks that influence contract terms: 1) Model licensing constraints for third-party weights (some can't be redistributed); 2) Latency delta if you require zero-caching for keys. Both will be called out in the tech appendix.

[08:22] Aaron: For the pilot, we want a test tenant with synthetic workloads that mimic our high-throughput trading queries. Can Redwood support spike loads?

[08:34] Nadia: Yes, we can provision a dedicated pool for pilot with configured autoscaling policies. We'll provide runbooks and a trial budget cap.

[08:46] Priya: Ok let's recap so procurement can close this in our notes.

[08:52] Elena: Recap: Redwood sends MSA redline and two DPA variants (standard and minimized retention) plus a short 'privileged keying' appendix and the technical annex on KMS/HSM and latency impact by 11/08. Legal-to-legal sync scheduled for 11/10. Helio to send preferred escrow/billing clause examples by 11/09. Pilot SOW and milestone payment proposal to be drafted after legal alignment; Marco to deliver benchmark note by 11/12.

[09:18] Evan: Sounds good. One more ask — please include a short sample SLA metric export in the redline bundle so our auditors can see how incidence reporting looks.

[09:30] Elena: We'll include that. Anything else?

[09:36] Priya: Not from procurement. Thanks everyone.

[09:42] Lindsey: We'll follow up after the legal sync if we need deeper security proofs.

[09:48] Elena: Great. We'll circle back post-sync. Thanks all.

Action items (verbatim in meeting):
- Elena: circulate redlined MSA and two DPA variant options (standard vs. minimized retention) — due 2025-11-08.
- Evan: send Helio's preferred escrow/billing language sample — due 2025-11-09.
- Marco: prepare short tech appendix on KMS/HSM flow and key custody diagram — due 2025-11-12.
- Nadia: add trial SLA monitoring dashboard access for Helio test tenant — due 2025-11-14.

References shared during call: Redwood MSA (link: https://redwood.example.com/msas/standard), DPA variants doc (link: https://redwood.example.com/dpa/variants), Tech appendix placeholder (internal link to be uploaded).

End of transcript.
